questions.question: What does Test-Driven Development involve?
questions.title: What is test-driven development?
questions.slide_text: What is test-driven development? Test Driven Development (TDD) is a practice advocated by agile software development methodologies, in which tests are written in advance of source-code development. These tests, intended to initially fail in the absence of any substantial implementation, effectively constitute a specification of the functionality and behavior of the software code, which can be tested as it is being developed Borle, Neil C., et al. "Analyzing the effects of test driven development in GitHub." Empirical Software Engineering 23.4 (2018): 1931-1958.

questions.question: What does the schema define in the context of testing component designs?
questions.title: How do schemas relate to testing components in different contexts?
questions.slide_text: How do schemas relate to testing components in different contexts? Let's say we are evolving designs for a drone propeller/ rotor setup The first part of the genetic encoding might represent the cross section of the blade The rest defines how many rotors there are, how big they are, etc. Say we have a schame like: 100100********... -> this defines a hyperplane of rotors with a certain cross section but with anything for the other characteristics of the rotor. So by exploring that hyperplane we test out that particular cross section with all other possible options for the design

questions.question: What does `model_target.predict(state_next_sample)` do?

questions.slide_text: Training Predict rewards for the s’ states achieved via the actions: future_rewards = model_target.predict(state_next_sample) Note that we are using the target model here Future rewards contains rewards for all possible actions so just get the max ones (i.e. most desired actions): tf.reduce_max( future_rewards, axis=1 )
